name: Khongjom War Memorial Complex
description: Memorial complex on Kheba Ching hill in Khongjom, Thoubal district, commemorating the decisive Battle of Khongjom (23 April 1891) during the Anglo-Manipur War. Features a tall sword monument, gardens, and tributes to Manipuri warriors including Major Paona Brajabasi who resisted British forces.
facts: Site of the last major battle of the Anglo-Manipur War of 1891
About 32-36 km southeast of Imphal on NH-102
Hosts annual Khongjom Day observances on 23 April
Includes world's tallest sword statue according to local sources

name: Waithou Lake (Waithou Pat)
description: Scenic freshwater lake in northern Thoubal district, formed by drainage from Waithou Hill and surrounding paddy fields. Known for pineapple cultivation on nearby slopes, former habitat of Ngaton fish, and boating/picnic opportunities with hill views.
facts: About 3 km from Thoubal HQ and 16 km from Imphal on Imphal-Moreh road
Historically a breeding ground for Ngaton fish before Cheksabi Barrage
Surrounded by hills and agricultural land
Official tourist interest site per district NIC

name: Ikop Pat (Ikop Lake)
description: Freshwater lake in western Athokpam and Khangabok areas of Thoubal district at about 772 m elevation. Saucer-shaped basin of roughly 13.5 km², culturally linked to the legendary Khamba-Thoibi story; important for local fisheries and birdlife despite pollution pressures.
facts: Linked to Khamba and Thoibi folklore
Supports migratory birds and local fishing

name: Thoubal
description: District headquarters and major trading town in the Manipur Valley, about 22 km from Imphal. Divided by NH-39/102, with the Thoubal River flowing through its centre; gateway for exploring local lakes, crafts, and historical sites.
facts: Thoubal River flows through the town

name: Thoubal River
description: Major river flowing east to west through the heart of Thoubal town and district, supporting agriculture, fisheries, and scenic views amid paddy fields. One of the key waterways of the eastern Manipur Valley.
facts: Flows through the centre of Thoubal town
Part of the district's wetland and drainage system
Accessible along the main highway corridor

name: Khangabok
description: One of the largest villages in Thoubal district (area ~20.5 km²), renowned for traditional Kouna (tule reed) handicrafts including mats, stools, and bags, as well as proximity to Ikop Pat. Agricultural hub with Meitei cultural practices.
facts: One of the largest villages in the district by area

name: Lousi Lake (Lousipat)
description: Significant freshwater wetland in Thoubal district covering around 18 km² historically, featuring a wetland ecosystem important for local water supply and fisheries. Partially reclaimed for agriculture but remains a scenic and ecological site near the Khongjom area.
facts: Approximate area historically over 18 sq km
Important local water and fishery resource
Part of the district's multiple lake system

name: Senapati (Tahamzam)
description: District headquarters of Senapati, a hill town at about 1,500 m elevation on the Imphal-Kohima highway. Locally known as Tahamzam (Hill of Butterflies) among Maram Nagas; commercial and administrative hub for the northern hill districts with markets and mixed tribal communities.
facts: About 62 km from Imphal on NH-2
Local name Tahamzam means Hill of Butterflies

name: Willong Khullen Megaliths
description: Remote Maram Naga village with over 130 prehistoric standing stones (menhirs) resembling Stonehenge, some up to 7 m tall. Erected for warrior feats, feasts of merit and celestial events; one of Manipur’s most important megalithic sites.
facts: Over 130 standing stones, some 4–7 m high
About 37 km from Maram on Maram-Peren road
Maram Naga village in Senapati district

name: Makhel Village
description: Sacred ancestral village of many Naga communities near the Nagaland border. Features the legendary banyan trees (believed grown from the Naga mother’s tomb), farewell monolith, triomonolith and other historical stones marking tribal dispersal.
facts: Believed ancestral homeland of Naga tribes
Sacred banyan trees and multiple monoliths
Near Mao and Dzukou Valley access
Official place of interest on district NIC site

name: Maram Khullen
description: One of the largest and oldest traditional villages of the Maram Naga tribe, retaining chieftainship, carved wooden houses and living cultural practices. Attractive for anthropologists and visitors seeking authentic hill-tribe heritage amid scenic ridges.
facts: Listed on official district places of interest

name: Mao
description: Border town and oldest hill station in Manipur on the Nagaland frontier, about 107 km from Imphal and 28 km from Kohima. Gateway for Dzukou Valley treks, with cool climate, historic inspection bungalow (1897) and vibrant Mao Naga culture.
facts: About 107 km from Imphal, 28 km to Kohima

name: Sadu Chiru Waterfall (Leimaram Falls)
description: Three-tiered waterfall near Ichum Keirap in the Sadar Hills area, with the main drop about 30 m into a clear pool. Popular picnic and nature spot amid forested foothills; short trek required. Officially listed under Senapati though near Bishnupur border.
facts: Official tourist place of Senapati district

name: Yangkhullen
description: Largest Zeme Naga village, built on a steep rocky slope about 47 km from Maram. Retains traditional social and economic life amid dramatic cliff landscapes; known for its hanging-village character and cultural authenticity.
facts: Largest Zemei village in the district

name: Purul
description: Village about 19 km from Maram on NH-39, home to indigenous games including Toutou and traditional wrestling during festivals. Scenic highland settlement with cultural practices and terraced fields.
facts: Famous for Toutou game and wrestling

name: Liyai
description: Village 33 km east of Tadubi featuring historical stone monoliths, water pools, banyan trees and traditional male/female houses. Origin point of the Barak River; culturally significant for local tribes.
facts: Listed on district NIC places of interest

name: Dzukou Valley (Manipur / Senapati Side)
description: High-altitude meadow valley of dwarf bamboo and seasonal wildflowers (including endemic Dzukou lily) at about 2,450 m, straddling the Senapati (Manipur)–Kohima (Nagaland) border. Accessed by trek from Mao; famous for winter snow and spring blooms. Flag: border with Nagaland; core often attributed to both.
